backstory:
Grukk fights for coin in the Crusher pits of Ieso, and he is professional enough to know exactly what each scar on him cost and what it earned. The orc war-bands here do not so much make war as invoice it: every bout has its purse, every wound its upkeep, every refusal-to-kill its bonus, and Grukk has learned to read that balance sheet as well as any quartermaster. They call him the Ledger for it, half in mockery and half in respect.

He was whelped in a war-band's baggage train and raised on the rules of the ring before the rules of the road, chiefly the first rule, that you do not kill a man who yields, because a dead opponent pays nothing and a grudge pays less. His clan-mother kept the band's books and beat sums into him alongside his footwork. He never knew a father he could name, only the long line of trainers who taught him to hit, to fall, and to rise looking as though it cost him nothing.

He is loud in the pit and quiet out of it, hoards his winnings, and dreams in his cheaper moments of buying a band of his own and never again bleeding for another orc's ledger.

Personality: gruff, calculating, oddly honest about money.
Mannerisms: cracks his knuckles one at a time, counting them off.
Appearance: a slab of scar-crossed muscle, tusks capped in cheap brass, a tally of bouts inked down one arm.
Flaws: greedy, and touchy about being thought stupid.
